Hi Grace —

Thanks for the outline. A few clarifying questions before we lock windows:

1) For EU data residency, will customer data be held in the EU node exclusively for all EU traffic, or do you plan to replicate to APAC for warmpath readiness? What are the guarantees around replication (if any)?
2) KMS — you mentioned customer-managed keys. Do we need an HSM connector or is Cloud KMS sufficient? Any impact on latency if we use our KMS?
3) Can you break down the egress/cross-region cost impact if failover traffic moves to APAC (we estimate peak burst ~20% of baseline).
4) Provisioning timeline: do you have blackout windows or preferred maintenance windows to avoid EU business hours (CEST)?

Happy to take a quick call. Lars (cc) will coordinate from ops.

Best,
Amelia Ross
VP Platform, Surgentia
amelia.ross@surgentia.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: EU node + APAC warmpath sequencing for renewal

Amelia —

Great questions, answers below (short form) — I'll open a follow-up ops write-up and loop Naomi for the runbook items.

1) Residency & replication: EU node will be the authoritative data path for EU-region traffic. We maintain an encrypted replica in APAC strictly for failover; replication is asynchronous and only used when your traffic is routed to APAC under the failover policy. Replication windows are configurable (default: near-real-time for KV caches, hourly snapshots for long-term store).

2) KMS: Cloud KMS integration is supported; for HSM-backed keys we have a connector option (customer HSM required). Latency impact for KMS operations is minimal; token-serving path uses local ephemeral keys after initial key handshake to avoid per-request KMS calls.

3) Egress/cross-region cost: worst-case egress on failover is estimated at 0.12 USD per 1k tokens beyond EU baseline. I asked Karthik to confirm numbers for the committed tier.

4) Provisioning windows: We prefer provisioning during early CET mornings (02:00–06:00 CEST) to minimize disruption. If you have strict blackout windows, we can adjust the schedule.

Attaching a draft provisioning schedule: eu-provisioning-schedule.docx

Would you be open to a 30-min call Friday 15th 09:00 CEST / 00:00 PDT?

Thanks —
Grace

Amelia, Grace —

Looping in the ops runbook excerpt and the pre-provision checklist. Key highlights:

- Pre-provision: signed SOW + PO, account KMS access details, SOC2 ATO checklist items (we'll snapshot once node is live)
- Network: customer to provide CIDR ranges for allowlist and confirm peering windows. We support AWS EU-West-1 and GCP europe-west4 for EU nodes.
- Cutover plan: staged traffic shifting with Canary (1%) -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over a 72-hour window; rollback triggers on latency or error thresholds
- Acceptance: post-provision load test (48 hours) with agreed TPS and p95 SLOs

Attachment: ops_runbook_eu_mirror.pdf

Short timeline: once SOW/PO received we target provision start in 2 business weeks and go-live in 6 weeks (dependent on peering sign-offs).
